ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders with retained photographs, with particular attention to cylinders 4-6 for vertical scoring and to the crosshatch condition.
DME over-rev and fault memory download, interpreted alongside a leakdown/compression test — never instead of the scope.
AOS function check (vacuum test) and inspection for oil mist in the intake tract and smoke on a cold start.
Cooling system: pressure test, inspect the 2023 water pump work, check the plastic coolant pipes and the radiators/condensers for debris and coastal corrosion.
Clutch engagement point, dual-mass flywheel rattle at idle, and transaxle shift quality across all six gears including 2nd cold.
Rear main seal / IMS area: inspect the bellhousing weep hole and record any oil residue; check for metallic debris in the oil filter media.
Suspension: rear control-arm and sway-bar bushings, front lower-arm bushings, shock condition, and confirm the new bump stops/dust covers are properly installed.
Rear tire date codes and any front/rear wear mismatch; verify TPMS function on all four corners.
Paint-depth readings on every panel to test the no-reported-accident Carfax, plus a lift inspection of the floorpan, jack points and front valence damage.
Confirm PCM, Bose, heated seats, spoiler deployment and climate control all operate.
what_would_change_verdict: A dated independent Porsche-specialist borescope with clean photos of cylinders 4-6, plus a clean DME over-rev report, would transform this from a gamble into a legitimate keeper candidate.
Invoice photographs for the 2023 cooling work, plus documented AOS and coolant-pipe service, would move documentation and condition materially upward.
A hammer price that stays inside the stated max price with fees included — unlikely given comps at $29,500-$34,500 — would fix the price-discipline problem.
Any borescope finding of scoring in 4-6, oil-consumption evidence, or a refusal to permit the scope before close should end interest immediately.
Evidence of a recent clutch/flywheel replacement with a receipt would remove one of the larger open 12-month costs.
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper the specification is close to ideal — a manual 987.1 Cayman S in Midnight Blue over Natural Brown is a car to hold, not a bridge — but it does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem the 335i is creating and it commits cash at a moment when cash preservation matters. It is only defensible if the borescope and over-rev report come back clean AND the hammer stays disciplined; without the scope it is not buyable at any price under this profile.
evidence.rationale: The decisive fact is what is not here: this is an M97 3.4 Cayman S and the listing contains no borescope, no cylinder photographs and no DME over-rev report, which the model profile treats as a hard requirement — seller silence on oil use is not evidence of clean bores. Everything else is encouraging: a lifelong California car, a Carfax snapshot with no reported damage, 5 owners and 21 service entries, and a narrative of real maintenance (water pump, thermostat and serpentine belt April 2023, brakes April 2024, oil March 2026, front tires, TPMS and front bump stops in 2026), though all of it appears as prose rather than as invoice images. The photographs support the condition story — deep Midnight Blue paint, straight panels, unmarked S wheels, a lightly worn Natural Brown interior and a rear underbody with only normal surface oxidation and no rust-through — while the seller himself discloses a hood chip, valence scratches and interior wear at the trunk trim, seatbelt and ignition. Rear tire age is unstated even though the fronts were replaced this year, so a matching rear pair should be budgeted. Logistics are as good as they get: Hawthorne is a day trip from Carmel, the dealer explicitly invites PPI and extra photos, and there are no additional dealer charges. The pricing is the second problem: at $25,000 with six days, an undisclosed reserve and comps at $25,750-$34,500 for similar-mileage S cars, the realistic hammer band is $29,000-$36,000 before the buyer fee, well past the max price in the state block. The catch-up bill is also ordinary-but-real for an 18-year-old 987: fluids, AOS if unknown, cooling inspection, rear tires, with clutch and coolant pipes lurking in the next twelve months. Net: an attractive, honestly presented car that cannot be bid on until the engine is scoped, and probably cannot be bought within budget even then.

critical_evidence.evidence: Seller posted a trunk-floor photo on request and describes 'two slight separations and a partial' at the spot welds, adding that he never inspected the area during 21 years of ownership and would leave it alone if keeping the car. That is a disclosed structural defect at the differential-mount/trunk-floor welds — the M's worst-known weak point — with no underside photos, no measurement, and no reinforcement work.

The only documented service is a July 2026 A/C compressor and drier job at 80,700 miles. No radiator, expansion tank, water pump, thermostat or hose records are shown for a 26-year-old S52; seller-reported items are limited to a 2026 battery and a 2024 oil change, both undocumented.
This is a 2000 car with the S52 engine (confirmed by VIN decode and listing), which predates the S54's rod-bearing and double-VANOS exposure, so rod-bearing records or oil analysis cannot apply.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: published VIN that decodes cleanly, factory build sheet in the gallery, itemised equipment, stated 21-year single ownership, a Carfax attached to the auction, named private seller answering questions, and walkaround/cold-start/top-demo videos. Maintenance and condition evidence is where it is nearly empty: one invoice (July 2026 A/C) covers the whole 21 years of the seller's tenure, with battery and oil changes only asserted. For an M car the two documents that set value — cooling-system work and subframe/trunk-floor repair — are absent, and the structural photo that does exist shows a defect rather than a fix.

condition.rationale: The car presents well cosmetically in the photos — straight bodywork, good gloss Imola Red, intact dash, correct Style 40 wheels — but the established defects are the expensive kind: confirmed trunk-floor spot-weld separations at the differential mount, 2019-date tires that must be replaced, a loose corner on the plexiglass soft-top window, hood chips, curb rash, and seat wear. Two panels were repainted specifically for the sale with no bodywork invoice or paint-depth data. Cooling system, VANOS, clutch, rear shock mounts and trailing-arm bushings are entirely unexamined here, and unknowns on a 26-year-old M pull this down rather than up.

price_value.rationale: Sold comps for 2000 M Roadsters at 75-80k miles cluster around $16,000-$17,250 (Kyle TX $16,000 at 76.9k; Zebulon NC $17,250 at 78.9k), with higher-mile cars at $10,000-$13,000. At the current $6,400 the bid is far under market, but it is a reserve auction, so the meaningful comparison is the likely hammer plus a Cars & Bids fee plus the known work: trunk-floor reinforcement, four tires and a top window. Priced at or below the low-$teens with those items priced in, it is fair value; priced at the top of the comp range it is paying keeper money for a car that needs its structure addressed and has no service file.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper the spec is right: factory manual, the more robust S52, LSD, Imola Red over black, a single owner since 2005, and the profile explicitly welcomes S52 M Roadsters. But the keeper case rests on documentation and structure, and this car has the structural defect disclosed and the documentation missing — exactly inverted from what raises long-term value on these. It is also not a bridge car for the 335i problem: it is a fair-weather second toy purchase that spends cash the accelerated_bridge plan wants preserved for a dependable daily.

logistics.rationale: Creedmoor, NC is a fly-out-and-drive-home or transport proposition, which is a cost line, not a risk. The real logistics problem is timing: the auction ends 2026-09-15 at 11:48 AM PDT, under a day out, so a Z3 M specialist inspection of the trunk floor and underside cannot realistically happen before money is committed. The seller is responsive and has been willing to take requested photos, which partly offsets it; California registration of a stock 2000 BMW should be routine.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Imola Red over black with the black top, S52, 5-speed, LSD, heated seats, Harman Kardon, one long-term owner, a Chris Bangle autograph and a wind baffle included — this is the charismatic fair-weather roadster the profile describes, and the colour is uncommon. Only the aftermarket shift knob and the worn driver's seat detract, and both are trivial to correct.

seller_questions: Can you post photos of the trunk floor from underneath the car — the differential mounting ears and both sides of the trunk pan — plus close-ups of each separated weld with a scale or tape measure in frame?

Does the soft top seal and operate fully through its cycle, and what exactly is loose on the plexiglass window corner — the bonding, the frame, or a tear?
Has the differential, gearbox or engine ever had fluid leaks or seal work, and is there any oil seepage from the valve cover or oil filter housing now?
ppi_focus: Trunk floor and differential-mount ears on a lift: map every separated spot weld, check for tearing into the pan, and get a specialist's written repair scope (reinforcement plates vs. monitoring).
Rear shock mount towers and rear trailing-arm (CAB) bushings, plus finned differential mount condition.
Cooling system by age and component: radiator, expansion tank neck, water pump, thermostat housing, hoses — pressure test cold and check for weeping.
Cold-start VANOS assessment and idle behaviour; scan for stored codes and check adaptations.
Paint-depth readings across the front bumper, right rear quarter and adjacent panels; inspect trunk and rear-wheel-arch seams for filler or prior collision repair.
Oil leak survey: valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, rear main, gearbox and diff seals.
Clutch engagement point, gearbox synchro feel in all gears, and driveshaft flex disc.
Soft top mechanism through a full cycle, rear plexiglass window mounting, and water test for leaks at the header and side rails.
Tire date codes verified in person (2019 expected) and wheel condition behind the curb rash; brake rotor thickness and pad life.
Rocker panels, floor pans and jack points for rust, and A/C output temperature after the 2026 compressor job.
what_would_change_verdict: A specialist PPI with a lift report bounding the trunk-floor repair, plus a firm written quote for reinforcement — with the hammer price discounted by that quote — moves this materially up.
Production of dated cooling-system invoices (radiator, expansion tank, water pump) and a real service file from the 21-year ownership would lift documentation from near-empty to credible.
Documented reinforcement work already performed, or evidence the separations are only surface sealer and not structural, would make this a legitimate keeper candidate.
Discovery that the separation extends into the trunk pan or diff ears, or paint-depth/panel evidence of unreported collision repair at the right rear quarter, moves it down decisively.
Winning at a price that implies keeper money (high-teens or above) without the structural scope priced in would turn a fair buy into a bad one.

condition.rationale: What is visible looks genuinely good: Imola Red paint with clean reflections and consistent panel gaps front and rear, unmarked factory M roadster wheels, tidy quad tips, uncracked dashboard, intact cluster display, and an interior consistent with 36k miles apart from normal creasing on the driver's seat bolster and cushion. But every item that actually decides a Z3 M's value is unexamined here: the rear subframe/diff-mount ears, the trunk-floor welds, cooling plastics, VANOS, motor and trans mounts, rear shock mounts, trailing-arm bushings, soft-top mechanism and A/C. A low odometer on a car this old often means aged rubber and plastics rather than a fresh car. Unknowns of this magnitude cap the rating in the middle.

price_value.rationale: At $28,998 all-in before tax and registration, this sits at or above the top of the S52 roadster market with none of the documentation that justifies a top price. A 30,959-mile 1998 is actively asking $21,353. The market notes are explicit that documentation, not mileage, drives value on these cars — and here mileage is the only argument. The Cars.com 'good deal' band is a market-average tool, not a condition-adjusted valuation.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper the car type is right: factory manual, S52 (the robust engine, no rod-bearing liability), Imola Red over black, low miles, clean reported history, and a genuinely characterful weekend car near the top of Jason's non-Porsche keeper list. Against that, the future_keeper mission demands genuine superiority backed by documentation, and this one offers the mileage but not the paperwork. It also does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem — it is a fair-weather two-seater, not a replacement daily for the 335i — and buying at this price consumes essentially the whole discretionary envelope while the BMW still needs resolving.

logistics.rationale: Tulsa, OK is roughly 1,700 miles from Carmel — a flight plus a two- to three-day drive home in a 25-year-old car whose cooling system has no documented history, or an enclosed transport cost. evidence.mission_note: As a future_keeper this is the right species of car — factory manual, S52 (no rod-bearing exposure), Imola Red, 36k miles, clean title — but the mission demands that a higher price be earned by documented superiority, and here the only documentation is identity and a history-report summary. It does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem, since a fair-weather two-seater cannot replace the 335i as a daily, so buying it at this number spends the whole discretionary envelope while leaving the bridge unsolved.
evidence.rationale: This is an attractive, correctly specified S52 M Roadster priced as though it were a documented one. The good news is real and verifiable: VIN [VIN] confirms a 2000 US Z3 M with the robust S52, which removes the S54 rod-bearing and double-VANOS liability that dominates 2001–2002 cars; the AutoCheck summary shows clean title and zero reported accidents; the odometer photo (~036,359) matches the advertised 36,362 miles; and the photos show glossy Imola Red paint, straight gaps, unmarked factory wheels, an uncracked dash and seats that wear consistent with the mileage. The bad news is that the profile's two decisive items for this model are entirely absent. There is no cooling-system documentation on a 25-year-old car whose plastics fail on age rather than mileage, and there is nothing at all — no underbody photo, no trunk-floor image, no lift inspection — covering the rear subframe and differential-mount ears, the failure that separates a $28,000 M Roadster from a project. A Honda franchise store's 'thoroughly inspected' boilerplate and a 1-month/1,000-mile warranty are not substitutes for either. Against the comps this is the top of the market: a 34,400-mile 2000 sold at $27,000 in July 2026, a 29,120-mile 1999 at $23,500 in August, and a 30,959-mile 1998 is asking $21,353 today. Documentation, not the odometer, is what earns a premium on these cars, and this listing has the odometer only. Everything hinges on a specialist lift inspection and on the price coming down toward what documented cars actually trade for.
evidence.next_action: Call South Pointe Honda and ask two questions before anything else: will they release the car to a named Tulsa BMW independent for a lift PPI focused on the rear subframe and cooling system, and what reconditioning work order and prior-owner records exist for stock YLC91663 — then book the inspection only if both answers are yes.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are solid: full VIN, stock number, decoded engine/drivetrain, equipment list, itemised price with doc fee, a published price history and an AutoCheck summary showing clean title / 0 accidents / multiple owners. Maintenance and condition evidence is completely absent: zero receipts, no records claim at all, no scan data, no inspection report, and the AutoCheck itself is a paywalled tile rather than an attached report. Strong on (a), empty on (b), and on a 166k-mile 1UR-FE the (b) side is what decides the car.

condition.rationale: What the photos show is encouraging: straight panels, even gaps, no visible body or rocker rust, glossy paint, factory alloys with usable tread, correct and even ride height, no sag at the rear. What they do not show is everything that matters on a salt-belt GX at 166k: frame rails, engine bay, cluster, interior, third row, tire date codes, and any evidence on the air-injection pump, valley plate or timing cover. Unknowns in exactly the model's weak spots hold this to below-average.

price_value.rationale: At $10,998 all-in before tax/registration this is under every comparable data point: a 2010 Base with 142,900 mi sold for $14,250, a 2012 Base at 162,800 mi brought $14,300, a 2013 Base at 203k brought $10,400, and a 173,709-mi 2010 in Modesto is asking $16,995. Cars.com's own band puts market at $12,376-$13,766. The $13,000 → $10,998 slide in eleven days says a CDJR store wants a Lexus trade-in off the lot, which is leverage. Risk-adjusted it still looks like value even if the air pump or KDSS bites, though the West-Coast price gap partly reflects Midwest rust discounting.

mission_fit.rationale: The GX460 genuinely supplies what the RX 350 does not: body-on-frame construction, full-time 4WD with low range, a tow rating, factory roof rails for a rooftop tent, and a flat load area behind a folding third row for dogs and camping gear. Automatic is fine for this branch and the Toyota V8 platform is the kind of thing his mechanic recommends. It loses points because it also duplicates the RX as a family hauler, because 166k on a non-documented example leans on the high-mileage rule that demands invoices rather than a low price, and because a Michigan car's underbody is a mission risk for a camping vehicle.

logistics.rationale: Farmington Hills is roughly 2,300 miles from Carmel, so this is a fly-out-and-drive or transport decision and a cost line, not a red flag. The positives: a physical franchise lot with posted hours, in a metro full of Toyota/Lexus independents, so a PPI is easy to arrange in principle — the group even owns a Suburban Toyota of Farmington Hills. The negatives: PPI permission is unstated, the selling store has no Lexus expertise, nothing addresses whether the car will pass California smog (the air-injection monitor is precisely the risk), and there is no help with title/registration for an out-of-state buyer.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Claret Mica over Ecru is an unusually handsome and period-correct GX combination, and the truck has real character — V8 burble, Land Cruiser Prado bones, a side-hinged tailgate. But it is a Base trim automatic SUV, explicitly not the enthusiast brief (MINI S / GTI / 128i / Z3 manual), and it is a second large Lexus in the driveway. It satisfies the utility branch, not the fun-car itch.

positives: Priced well under every comparable: $10,998 all-in versus $14,250 for a 142,900-mi 2010 Base and $14,300 for a 162,800-mi 2012 Base, with the dealer cutting $2,002 in eleven days — clear negotiating leverage on a Lexus trade-in at a CDJR store.

Correct platform for the utility_capability mission: body-on-frame Prado underpinnings, 4.6L 1UR-FE V8, full-time 4WD with low range, tow capability, factory roof rails and a folding third row — capability the RX 350 does not have.
Identity is fully pinned: VIN, stock number, decoded engine/series, equipment list and an itemised all-in price, with an AutoCheck summary of clean title and zero reported accidents.
Exterior presents well in the photos — straight panels, even gaps, no visible rocker or wheel-arch rust, level stance, unmodified factory alloys and running boards.
Toyota/Lexus drivetrain is exactly the brand his mechanic recommends, and 1UR-FE V8s routinely run past 250k with basic maintenance.
Fixed-price dealer sale at a physical lot inside a large metro, so an independent PPI and a same-week purchase are both practical if permission is granted.
concerns: Observed: a 16-year-old Michigan salt-belt vehicle with 166,024 miles and no underbody, frame-rail or brake-line photographs anywhere in the attached set — frame rust is the profile's named deal-breaker for non-western cars and nothing here addresses it.

Observed: zero maintenance evidence of any kind — no records claim, no invoices, no inspection — on a non-Toyota-badged 166k car, which is precisely the situation the high-mileage rule says must be answered with documented major renewal rather than a low price.

Unverified: 1UR-FE valley-plate coolant leak and timing-cover seepage (ask for clear engine-bay photos of the valley area and both timing-cover seams, cold and after a drive) — Jason is already living with one unresolved coolant leak on the BMW.

Unverified: warning-light and code status, tire date codes, transfer-case actuator function and 4LO engagement (no cluster photo, no scan, no sidewall images).

seller_questions: Will you email the complete AutoCheck PDF (not the summary tiles), showing every title, state and ownership event with dates and mileages?
Can you run a full OBD-II scan and send photographs of the results, including all emissions readiness monitors and any stored or pending codes, specifically P2440/P2442?

Can you send ten clear underbody photographs taken on a lift: both frame rails front and rear, the rear crossmember and spring perches, the transfer case and driveshaft area, brake and fuel lines, and both rocker seams?
Does this truck have KDSS? If it does, please photograph the KDSS accumulators and hydraulic lines and confirm they are dry.
Please photograph the engine bay with the intake area visible: the valley between the heads, both timing-cover seams, and the coolant reservoir level.
What exactly did the $499 reconditioning cover — can you send the internal repair order with line items and the mileage it was performed at?
Did the trade-in come with any service records or a Lexus/Toyota dealer service history you can pull by VIN?
Can you send photographs of all four tire sidewalls showing the DOT date codes, plus measured tread depths, and confirm the brands match?
Will you send a cold-start video: key on, first 60 seconds of idle, the full cluster visible at start-up and after the lights clear, and the air pump audible?
Will you allow a pre-purchase inspection at an independent Lexus/Toyota specialist of my choosing, or at your own Suburban Toyota of Farmington Hills store, before any deposit?
Will you road-test it and confirm 4WD low range engages and disengages normally and that the transfer case actuator does not throw a code?
What is the exact out-the-door number for an out-of-state California buyer, and will you state in writing that the vehicle is sold with no active check-engine light?
ppi_focus: Frame rails, rear crossmember, spring perches, brake and fuel lines on a lift — structural rust assessment on a Michigan vehicle, with a pick test on any scaled areas.
Secondary air injection system: live data on the pump and switching valves, emissions readiness monitors driven to complete, and history of P2440/P2442.
1UR-FE valley plate and both timing covers inspected for coolant and oil seepage; coolant pressure test and reservoir condition.
Confirm KDSS fitment; if present, inspect accumulators, lines and cylinders for weeping and measure cross-axle lean.
AVS / rear load-levelling shocks for leakage and correct ride-height response; all control-arm, trailing-arm and sway-bar bushings.
Transfer case actuator operation, 4LO engagement, front and rear differential fluid condition and any housing weeping.
Transmission fluid condition and shift quality under load, plus a scan for stored transmission codes.
Tire DOT date codes, tread depth, matching, and brake pad/rotor measurement.
Evidence of towing use: hitch wear, rear spring sag, transmission cooler, trailer wiring condition.
Interior and third row function, sunroof drains and headliner for water staining, all seat heat/ventilation functions.
what_would_change_verdict: A lift-based PPI by a Lexus/Toyota independent showing a clean frame and underbody, with completed emissions readiness monitors and no air-injection codes, would move this from speculative to a strong pragmatic buy at this price.
Documented service history — plugs, ATF, transfer case and differential fluids, coolant — or an air-injection pump replacement invoice would answer the high-mileage rule directly.
Confirmed frame rust, a stored P2440/P2442, or a wet valley plate would drop it out of contention; this buyer should not import a second coolant problem or a smog-check failure.
Refusal to allow an outside PPI or to send underbody photographs before a deposit should end the conversation regardless of price.
A comparable West-Coast GX460 with records at $14,000-$17,000 — the Modesto car, for example, if it inspects well — would likely beat this one on total risk even at a higher sticker.
evidence.mission_note: This is a legitimate utility_capability candidate rather than a duplicate of the RX: body-on-frame, low range, a tow rating and roof rails give it the camping and gear capability the RX lacks, and the automatic is appropriate here. But it fits the mission only as a pragmatic, documentation-light purchase — in accelerated_bridge mode the accelerant is the BMW's unreliability, and buying an undocumented 166k-mile salt-belt truck sight-unseen would swap one unknown coolant problem for another.
evidence.rationale: Priced at $10,998 all-in, this GX460 is the cheapest credible example in the comp set — under the $14,250 paid for a 142,900-mile 2010 Base and the $14,300 for a 162,800-mile 2012 Base — and the dealer's $13,000-to-$10,998 slide in eleven days signals a franchise CDJR store wanting a Lexus trade off the lot. Identity and terms are well documented: VIN, stock number, decoded 4.6L V8 and 4WD, a full equipment list, an itemised price, and an AutoCheck summary reading clean title with zero reported accidents. Condition evidence is the opposite: the attached photos show straight, gloss-red bodywork with no visible rocker or arch rust and a level stance, but there is not one underbody, engine-bay, cluster or interior image, and the ad offers no records claim at all. That matters because all four model-critical items come back missing — secondary air injection on the exact 2010-2012 P2440/P2442 population, KDSS fitment and leak status, frame rust on a 16-year-old Michigan vehicle, and warning-light status. The high-mileage rule applies squarely at 166,024 miles: a low price is not the convincing case, invoices are. A Farmington Hills location is a cost and an inspection-access question, not a flag, and the dealer group's own Suburban Toyota store sits in the same town, so a competent PPI should be arrangable. Two specific unknowns carry real money here — an air-injection pump that also blocks California smog, and frame corrosion that no discount repairs — so the sequence is evidence first, negotiation second.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer requesting three things before any deposit: the full AutoCheck PDF, a photographed full OBD-II scan with emissions readiness monitors, and ten lift photographs of the frame rails, rear crossmember and brake lines — then, if those are clean, book a pre-purchase inspection at an independent Lexus/Toyota specialist in the Farmington Hills area.

documentation.rationale: Everything of substance is seller prose in capital letters: 'SERVICED', 'BRAND NEW CLUTCH', 'ONLY 65K ORIGINAL MILES'. No invoices, no dates, no mileages, no service book, no undercarriage or trunk-floor photos. The only third-party item is an AutoCheck summary (clean title, 0 accidents, 'multiple' owners), which the buyer has not yet seen in full. On these cars the profile is explicit that documentation matters more than mileage, and there is essentially none.

condition.rationale: The one captured photo shows a straight, clean silver car on correct factory M double-spoke wheels with good panel gaps, intact front bumper and side vents, and no obvious cosmetic distress. That is all that is established. The rear subframe/trunk-floor area, cooling system, top mechanism, cluster pixels, dash, VANOS, and tire date codes are all unexamined, and unknowns on a 26-year-old M pull this down hard. A claimed new clutch with no receipt neither helps nor is counted.

price_value.rationale: $19,950 all-in (dealer confirms no extra fees) for a 65,718-mile S52 roadster sits at or slightly below the recent sold band: $20,000 for a 55.6k-mile car (Cars & Bids, Jul 2026), $23,000 for a 62,863-mile car (Utah, May 2026), $17,900 for a 77k-mile car, $23,500 for a 29k-mile BaT car. Fair market, not a steal, and the price carries zero documentation premium — with subframe and cooling status unknown, a buyer must reserve $3-5k of catch-up plus the risk of a $2-4k reinforcement job, which erodes the 'Great Deal' label. Cheaper live auction peers exist at $5.5-12.5k, though condition unknown.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper this is exactly the right shape: factory manual, S52 (the robust engine, no rod-bearing liability), LSD, clean title, 65k miles, and Jason explicitly likes Z3 M roadsters. But it is a fair-weather two-seat weekend car, not a replacement for the ailing 335i's daily duty, and buying it does not resolve the accelerated_bridge problem while consuming most of the ideal budget. It also conflicts with cash preservation: it is attractive only as a keeper.

logistics.rationale: Feasterville-Trevose, PA is roughly 2,900 miles from Carmel — fly-and-drive or ~$1,300-1,800 enclosed/open transport, a cost, not a risk. The real friction is inspectability: 'by appointment only, we have several locations' means the car may not be where the ad implies, and PPI access is unstated. A specialist E36/7 M inspection (Philadelphia area has good BMW indies) must be arranged and confirmed in writing before money moves. Registration in CA is feasible (OBD-II, must pass smog on transfer) but unverified.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Silver over black with the black top is the common, slightly anonymous M Roadster spec rather than a standout (Estoril, Imola, Cosmos with red or dual-tone interior). But the car itself — S52, five-speed, LSD, heated seats, stock wheels, no visible mods — is honest, correct, and characterful, and the roadster is the version he can drive on the Monterey coast year-round. The coupe is the more special body style he also covets.

contradictions.detail: Facebook header states 'Driven 192,000 miles' while the seller's own description says '190k miles maintained with care'. Likely rounding, but the two figures in the same ad do not match and no odometer photo is provided.

critical_evidence.evidence: The 2010-2012 GX460 secondary air injection pump/valve failure (P2440/P2442) is the single most expensive known fault on this car and the ad's mechanical list does not mention pumps, valves, codes or a scan. No OBD scan photo attached.

KDSS is advertised as a feature and an Ironman kit was installed over it, which is exactly the situation where KDSS leaks and cross-corner lean show up. No photos of the KDSS valve body/accumulators, no lean measurement, no install invoice.

No underbody, frame rail or KDSS-area photos in the attached set. Southern California history implies low risk but nothing establishes the frame's condition at 192k miles with off-road use shown in the trail photos.
No photo of a lit instrument cluster or of a running dash; the interior photos show the cluster off or obscured. Ad attribute 'no significant damage or problems' is seller prose, not a scan.

documentation.rationale: Weak on both halves. Identity and terms: no VIN, no odometer photo, no title photo — only a Facebook attribute set (clean title, 2 owners, 192k) and a named private seller with a rating history; the equipment description is detailed and the photos confirm most of it. Maintenance and condition evidence: essentially zero — a bullet list of claimed work (radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters) with no dates, no mileages, no invoices, no scan, no service history, and no documentation of the suspension install. At 192,000 miles the claim list is the least persuasive form of evidence available.

condition.rationale: Photos genuinely look good: straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows with no bolster collapse or cracked dash, working nav/ML/RSE hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws with real tread, tidy rack and hitch. Against that, this is a 192k-mile first-year GX460 with the three expensive model faults — secondary air injection, KDSS, valley-plate/timing-cover coolant seepage — entirely unaddressed in the ad, plus a lift of unknown install quality on a KDSS chassis, and no underhood, undercarriage or cold-start evidence. Trail photos show the car has actually been used off pavement. Unknowns dominate the areas that cost the most.

price_value.rationale: The asking price is far off the market. A 2010 Premium with 173,709 miles is asking $16,995 in Modesto; a 2010 Premium with 230,000 miles sold for $9,800 in Escondido; a 142,900-mile 2010 sold for $14,250 on Cars & Bids; and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same money as this 2010 with 192,000 miles. Bolt-ons (Ironman kit, rack, AT tires, traction boards) recover pennies on the dollar at resale and, per Jason's brief, add modest value at most. The ad has sat nine weeks at one price with no reduction, which is itself market feedback.

mission_fit.rationale: The capability case is real: body-on-frame, low range, locking centre diff, KDSS, Crawl Control, a full-length roof rack that suits a rooftop tent, a hitch, and a third row — all things the RX 350 cannot supply. But this is also a second large Lexus SUV in the driveway, it is a 192k-mile example rather than a low-risk one, and the mission requires it to justify the overlap on capability and dependability. A cheaper, lower-mileage GX would satisfy the same mission with far less exposure.

logistics.rationale: Mission Viejo is roughly 330 miles from Carmel — a one-day drive or a short flight, and Jason will drive a good car home. Southern California means abundant Toyota/Lexus and GX-specialist shops for a PPI including a KDSS-aware inspection, and the seller has a 20-rating marketplace history. Offsets: PPI access is not addressed in the ad, no VIN is published so nothing can be pre-checked, and a California private-party sale requires the seller to supply a current smog certificate, which is unstated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grey over beige with wood trim, Mark Levinson, rear entertainment and a tasteful mild overland build is an attractive, coherent package and photographs well on a fire road. It is also an automatic V8 SUV and makes no claim on the enthusiast brief (MINI/GTI/128i/Z3); its appeal is competence and family utility, not character Jason is chasing.

positives: Genuinely capable spec the RX 350 lacks: KDSS, Crawl Control, low range, full-length roof rack suited to a rooftop tent, hitch and a power third row.
Photographic condition is strong for the mileage — straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows, uncracked dash, intact nav/Mark Levinson/RSE hardware.
Southern California car with a matching set of Falken Wildpeak AT3W all-terrains and a level, modest lift rather than a big cheap one.
Toyota 1UR-FE/J150 platform is exactly what Jason's mechanic recommends and parts/specialist support in California is excellent.
Private seller with a long-standing, highly rated marketplace account within a day's drive, so a specialist PPI before money moves is straightforward to arrange.
concerns: Observed: the price is out of step with the comps — $23,995 for a 192,000-mile 2010 when a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 and a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995; it has sat nine weeks with no reduction.
Observed: an Ironman 4x4 lift has been installed over a KDSS chassis with no install invoice, alignment sheet or lean measurement, and the trail photos confirm the truck has been used off pavement.

Unverified: KDSS leak or cross-corner lean (inspect the valve body, accumulators and sway-bar cylinders for weep and measure lean on level ground).
Unverified: 1UR-FE valley-plate and timing-cover coolant seepage, plus frame and underbody condition (request underhood and undercarriage photos and a lift inspection).

seller_questions: What is the VIN, and will you send a photo of the title and current registration?
Can you send a photo or printout of a full OBD scan showing stored and pending codes plus readiness monitors, taken in the last week?
Has the secondary air injection system ever thrown P2440/P2442 or been repaired? If repaired, whose invoice and at what mileage?
Who installed the Ironman kit, on what date and at what mileage, and do you have the invoice and post-install alignment printout?
Was KDSS disconnected or re-shimmed during the lift, and can you photograph the KDSS valve body and both sway-bar cylinders for leaks?
Why were the radiator and thermostat replaced — was there a leak or an overheat event — and can you send those receipts with dates and mileage?
Have the transmission, transfer case and front/rear differential fluids been changed, and at what mileage?
Can you send photos of the engine valley/rear of the intake area and of the frame rails and underbody taken on a lift or from underneath?
Will you meet me at a Toyota/Lexus or GX specialist of my choosing in Orange County for a two-hour PPI on the lift before any money moves?
Do you have a current California smog certificate, and will the sale include one?
What are the DOT date codes on the four Falken tires, and do you have the purchase receipt?
Can you send a cold-start video of at least two minutes, from key-on, with the instrument cluster in frame?
ppi_focus: Secondary air injection: scan for P2440/P2442, check pump operation on cold start and inspect the valves/pump for moisture intrusion.
KDSS: inspect valve body, accumulators and both sway-bar cylinders for hydraulic weep; measure cross-corner lean on level ground and confirm the system still articulates after the lift.
1UR-FE coolant: inspect the valley plate area, timing cover and water pump for seepage; pressure-test the cooling system and check for oil/coolant cross-contamination.
Frame rails, crossmembers and skid areas from below for rust, impact damage or bent components from off-road use.
Lift installation quality: control-arm and shock mounting, CV boot and axle angle, driveshaft/carrier bearing, brake and ABS line routing, and steering geometry/alignment specs.
Transfer case actuator function: shift into 4-Lo and back, confirm no fault codes and no grinding.
Suspension bushings, ball joints, tie rods and rear shocks at 192k miles.
Automatic transmission: fluid condition and level via the check procedure, road-test for shift quality and torque-converter lockup shudder.
Tire DOT date codes and irregular wear pattern that would reveal alignment issues after the lift.
Full body/paint meter check and panel-gap review for unreported collision repair, since no history report exists.
what_would_change_verdict: A clean specialist PPI plus a full scan with no codes, documented healthy KDSS with no lean, and dry valley plate/timing cover — combined with a price renegotiated toward the $15,000-17,000 band the comps support.
Production of dated invoices for the air-injection system, drivetrain fluids and the lift install, converting the claim list into records.
The VIN and a clean history report confirming two owners, no accidents and completed recall work.
Downward: any P2440/P2442 code, visible KDSS hydraulic weep or measurable lean, or coolant seepage at the valley plate — each is four figures on top of an already over-market ask.
Downward: seller declining to release the VIN or to allow a PPI at an independent shop.
evidence.mission_note: This does deliver capability the RX 350 genuinely lacks — body-on-frame, low range, KDSS, roof rack for a rooftop tent, hitch and a third row — so it clears the overlap test on paper. But at 192,000 miles with the three expensive GX460 faults entirely undocumented and an asking price at the level of a 2017 with 64,000 fewer miles, it is not the low-risk capability buy the accelerated_bridge mode calls for at this number.
evidence.rationale: The verdict is driven by price and evidence, not by the truck itself. Condition in the photos is legitimately good: straight grey paint, clean beige leather across three rows, intact Mark Levinson and rear-entertainment hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws and a level, modest lift. But the ad's entire mechanical case is a bullet list — radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters — with no date, mileage or invoice behind a single line, and at 192,000 miles that is the weakest possible support. Every one of the four model-critical items is missing: no scan for P2440/P2442 secondary air injection, no KDSS leak or lean check on a chassis that has had an Ironman kit installed over it, no underbody or frame images, and no lit-cluster or cold-start evidence. No VIN is published, so no history report, recall check or decode is possible. The market is unambiguous: a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995 in Modesto, a 142,900-mile 2010 sold at $14,250, a 230,000-mile one sold at $9,800, and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same as this. Nine weeks at $23,995 with no reduction confirms the market's read. The build is a modest positive at best under Jason's own rule that accessories never substitute for evidence.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a recent full OBD scan photo (stored and pending codes), the Ironman install invoice with alignment sheet, and confirmation he will meet at a GX/Toyota specialist in Orange County for a lift PPI — and open the price conversation at the $15,000-17,000 the comps support before booking anything.

Clutch: engagement height, slip under third-gear roll-on, judder from rest, plus inspection for slave/master cylinder leakage
Engine mounts and gearbox mount: check idle vibration through the shifter and steering wheel, and inspect for collapsed or oil-soaked rubber
Oil leaks: valve cover/oil filter housing gaskets, oil pan, and any residue on the underside of the engine and subframe
Suspension: front strut mounts, control-arm bushings, drop links, and a four-wheel alignment check for prior curb or pothole damage

evidence.mission_note: This is the right car for the enthusiast-bridge mission on spec — a low-mile, clean-title, California, manual F56 Cooper S available immediately and 130 miles from home — but at roughly $19.5-20k all-in it sits about a third above the $15k mission intent, and it arrives with essentially no verified maintenance evidence. It fits the brief emotionally and on resale; it fails it on price discipline unless the dealer moves or documents real work.
evidence.rationale: Verdict pressure here is price and documentation, not the car. The configuration is the profile's stated bullseye: 2018 F56 Cooper S, six-speed manual, White Silver with white roof, pano, sport seats, harman/kardon, 51,822 miles, clean title, 0 reported accidents, 2 owners, sitting on California plates at a dealer a two-hour drive from Carmel. The evidence base behind that, however, is one AutoCheck summary line and a single front-quarter photo; there are no service records, no engine-bay or dash images, and no mention of tires, cooling work or ECU history. Both model-critical keys — cooling_history and tune_status — are missing outright, which matters because the B46 cooling plastics and undisclosed tunes are the two ways this generation quietly costs money. The windshield grease-pen and service sticker in the photo say this is a fresh trade at a Ford store that has not finished recon, so nothing has been proven fixed. On money, CarGurus itself calls $18,076 a $146-above-market 'fair deal,' meaning fee-inclusive retail with no cushion; add CA tax and registration and the buyer is near $20k on a mission scoped under $15k. Logistics and inspectability are the strongest part of the file: an in-state dealer car makes a specialist PPI and smog straightforward if they cooperate. Treat this as a real candidate contingent on a clean specialist PPI and a materially better out-the-door number, not as a buy on the strength of the ad.
evidence.next_action: Call the dealer and ask, in one conversation, for (a) written agreement to an off-site independent MINI/BMW specialist PPI before any deposit, (b) the full AutoCheck PDF and recon worksheet, and (c) a firm out-the-door number for a Monterey County buyer — then book the PPI only if all three come back acceptable.

contradictions.topic: odometer reading vs Carfax last reported
contradictions.detail: Listing states 83k miles on the digital odometer while the Carfax snapshot shows 75,208 as the last REPORTED reading. These are compatible (the report entry predates ~8k of recent driving), but the gap should be reconciled against the full report.
Tracker read 'Automatic'; the listing specifies a seven-speed PDK dual-clutch transaxle. Corrected in facts; not a listing contradiction.

critical_evidence.evidence: Seller states he performed the PDK fluid/filter service himself in his home shop in 2022 (~8k miles ago) and explicitly says 'I do not have any other service records.' No dated invoice, parts receipt, or fluid documentation offered.
No borescope images, leakdown or compression sheet provided for this 16-year-old flat-six. DFI mitigates bore-score risk relative to 987.1 but does not remove the value of the test.

The check engine light is illuminated and the seller attributes it to the high-flow cats, but no PIWIS/Durametric printout, code number, overrev report (ranges 1-6) or readiness-monitor status is shown — precisely the data a modified, possibly track-driven car needs.

Aftermarket high-flow catalytic converters are welded into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO cited; the CEL is on and the seller confirms SC has no inspections and that he 'never explored' spacers. No photos of the cats/manifolds and no statement that OE units were retained.

A bidder asked directly about water pump, belts and cooling system; the seller replied he has no other service records. No water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, radiator or condenser receipts, and no photos of the front radiator area with ducts removed.

Bilstein PSS9 coilovers and Tarett rear toe control arms are fitted; no installation invoice, no ride-height/damper-setting record, no four-wheel alignment sheet, and no close photos of the shock bodies for seal leakage. A commenter's question about correct Bilstein settings is unanswered in the captured text.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are solid: full VIN that decodes correctly to a 2010 Cayman S 3.4, a detailed equipment list, named private seller, location, live bid history and a Carfax snapshot showing no reported accidents and 4 prior owners. Maintenance and condition evidence is essentially absent: the seller states in writing that he has no service records beyond his own home-shop work, the 2022 PDK service and plugs are recollection only, there are no cooling-system, suspension or alignment invoices, no scan report for an actively illuminated CEL, and no borescope or leakdown. On a 16-year-old, visibly modified Porsche this is the weakest half of the category and it is empty.

condition.rationale: Cosmetically the car presents well in the photos — straight Arctic Silver panels, clean black leather, unmarked 18" Cayman S II wheels, red calipers, a dry-looking rear subframe and transaxle in the lift shot. Against that: an illuminated check engine light, non-compliant cats welded into the manifolds, Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors (unusable street pads), mismatched Michelin front / Continental rear tires of unknown date, PSS9 coilovers of unknown age and seal condition, a harness bar, and zero documentation for water pump, thermostat, radiators, bushings or clutch-side wear items at 83k miles and 16 years. Seller says no track use in his 4 years but cannot speak for the prior three owners, and the hardware set is the profile's classic track-history signature.

price_value.rationale: Bidding is $22,750 with a day to run, inside the ideal band on paper — but the profile is explicit that a PDK car with aftermarket cats, coilovers, a harness bar and a CEL is a 15-25% discount-tier asset, and that discount is already priced into where this will likely land. Layer on known work this listing itself establishes (restoring compliant catalysts, replacing track pads/rotors, correcting the mismatched tires) plus undocumented cooling and PDK service, and the risk-adjusted value is thin. Resale in 6-24 months is the weak point: a modified silver-over-black PDK with a smog problem is the slowest-selling combination in the model, not the easy flip the mission wants.

mission_fit.rationale: The mission requires a manual; this is a PDK, and it does not win the pragmatic_bridge exception because it loses on reliability evidence, condition documentation and — decisively — convenience: welded-in non-CARB cats with an active CEL make California registration a project before the car is even usable. It is also not the immediately available, low-cost, dependable bridge that the sick 335i argues for. A 987.2 Cayman S is a wonderful Highway 1 car, but this specific example is the discount, unevidenced end of it.

logistics.rationale: Greer, SC is a straightforward fly-and-drive or BaT shipping proposition and distance itself is only a cost. The real logistics problem is timing and access: the auction closes within a day, no PPI has been arranged, no Porsche-specialist inspection or scan report is on offer, and money moves before anyone can look at it. Then California smog: aftermarket cats without an EO and an illuminated CEL mean referee/registration work before the car can be plated in Carmel.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Mid-engine, hydraulic steering, Sport Chrono, LSD, a proper flat-six soundtrack and a genuinely usable two-trunk layout — the character is there and Jason likes Porsches. But Arctic Silver over black is the most common and least differentiated 987.2 combination, PDK removes the manual engagement he explicitly wants, and the harness bar, track pads and coilovers give it a used-hard tuner flavour rather than the clean, documented specialist-serviced car the profile says to buy.

known_work_items: Restore CARB-compliant catalytic converters / manifold assemblies for California registration ($2,000-$4,000)
Diagnose and clear the illuminated CEL and complete readiness monitors for smog ($200-$500)
Replace Hawk HP Plus track pads (and likely the slotted rotors) with OE-spec street pads and rotors ($1,200-$1,800)
Correct mismatched Michelin front / Continental rear tires to a matched staggered set ($1,400-$2,000, DOT dates unverified)
Four-wheel alignment on the coilover-equipped chassis, no alignment sheet provided ($200-$400)
positives: Correct 987.2 DFI 3.4 S drivetrain — the generation that sheds the IMS and bore-scoring anxiety of the 987.1 — with LSD and Sport Chrono, factory 320 hp.

Presents very cleanly in the photos: straight Arctic Silver bodywork, tidy black leather with no sticky-trim or torn bolster visible, unmarked 18" Cayman S II wheels, and a lift shot of a dry, undamaged rear subframe and transaxle area.
Cooperative, candid private seller who answers questions quickly and does not overstate — he openly admits he has no service records and that SC has no emissions inspections.
Carfax snapshot reports no accidents or damage, an Actual Mileage title in the seller's name, and four years / ~8k miles of stable recent ownership.
Chassis mods are quality parts (Tarett toe links, Bilstein PSS9, Soul tips) rather than junk, and the car sits and looks right.
concerns: Observed: the check engine light is illuminated and the aftermarket high-flow cats are WELDED into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO — for a car to be registered in Carmel this is a smog and registration problem requiring compliant catalysts, not a cosmetic annoyance, and the seller confirms he never pursued a fix because SC has no inspections.

Observed: PDK, not a manual. The mission requires a manual and the profile is explicit that manual commands a widening premium on 987.2 Caymans while PDK cars sell slower — this hurts both the brief and the 6-24 month resale.

Observed: the seller states in writing he has no service records other than his own home-shop work; the 2022 PDK fluid/filter service, plugs and annual oil changes are recollection only, with nothing dated for the prior 75k miles and three owners.

Observed: Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors, a harness bar, PSS9 coilovers and Tarett toe links — the exact package the profile says signals track history and pushes a car into the discount tier; the seller can only vouch for his own four years.
Observed: mismatched tire brands front to rear (Michelin and Continental) with no DOT dates given on a 16-year-old car.

Unverified: nothing on the cooling system — no water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or radiator work is documented at 83k miles and 16 years, and a bidder's direct question about it drew 'no other service records' (ask for the pump vent-hole and front radiator photos with ducts removed).
unknowns: The actual stored DTC(s) and a full PIWIS/Durametric scan, including the overrev report ranges 1-6 — the single most informative document for a car with this hardware set.
Whether the original catalytic converters/manifolds were retained and are included, and whether any CARB-legal path exists for the installed units.
Any dated invoice for water pump, thermostat, coolant service, expansion tank or radiator/condenser work in the car's life.
DOT date codes on all four tires and the exact sizes/brands per axle.
Age, mileage and rebuild status of the Bilstein PSS9 dampers, current ride height/damper settings, and whether a four-wheel alignment was done after the Tarett toe links.
Prior-owner track history (three owners before 2022) — event logs, corner-balance or alignment records, brake-duct or harness evidence.
Borescope/leakdown condition of all six cylinders and any cold-start smoke (AOS/RMS).
Whether a Porsche-specialist PPI can be completed before the auction closes.
seller_questions: Please post a photo of the scan tool screen showing the exact stored DTC number(s) and the OBD readiness monitor status, plus the overrev report from a PIWIS or Durametric session.
Do you still have the original OEM catalytic converters and manifold assemblies, and will they be included with the car?
You said the cats are welded into the factory manifolds — can you post close photos of that weld area and of the O2 sensor bungs?
Can you post the parts receipt (fluid, filter, gasket) from the 2022 PDK service you performed, with the date and the odometer reading at that time?

Has the water pump, thermostat, coolant expansion tank or either radiator ever been replaced? If you don't know, will you post photos of the pump vent hole area and of the front radiators with the ducts removed?
What are the DOT date codes and sizes on all four tires — please photograph each sidewall.
When were the PSS9 coilovers installed, how many miles are on them, and can you photograph all four shock bodies for seal weeping?
Was a four-wheel alignment performed after the Tarett toe links went in? Please post the alignment sheet.
Is the car currently set to the Bilstein-recommended ride height, and what damper settings are dialled in front and rear?

Will you allow a Porsche independent specialist near Greer to put the car on a lift for a borescope and leakdown before the auction closes, and can you accommodate the appointment in the time remaining?
Can you post a cold-start video from a full overnight sit, showing the first 60 seconds from behind and the gauge cluster?
Does the deployable rear spoiler raise and lower correctly with no fault, and do all door locks and the alarm/immobilizer behave normally after the car sits a week?
ppi_focus: Full PIWIS/Durametric scan: all stored and pending codes, overrev ranges 1-6, PDK adaptation values and fault memory, readiness monitors.
Catalyst/exhaust inspection: confirm what is welded where, whether OE manifolds are recoverable, and price the return to CARB-compliant units for California registration.
PDK behaviour: low-speed engagement judder, 1-2 shift delay, clutch-pack adaptation data — the 2022 self-performed service is the only claimed fluid change.
Cooling system: water pump vent hole for weeping, pink crust on the block, expansion tank seam and cap, front radiators and condensers with ducts removed for debris packing and corrosion.
Borescope all six cylinders plus a leakdown, and check the bellhousing and RMS area for oil weep and the AOS for cold-start smoke.
Suspension: PSS9 shock bodies for seal leakage and age, Tarett toe link condition and torque, front lower control arm bushings and top mounts, then a corner-weight-aware four-wheel alignment.
Brakes: measure Frozen rotor thickness and condition, confirm Hawk HP+ pad wear and any heat-cracking or bluing that would indicate track use.
Tire DOT dates and sizes on all four corners; confirm the staggered set is correct for the car.
Track-use forensics: harness bar mounting, seat rail and floor for bolt marks, brake duct evidence, rollbar drill holes, and undertray/diffuser scrapes.
Deployable spoiler mechanism operation and a parasitic-draw test given the model's known ignition switch, immobilizer and door-actuator drains.
what_would_change_verdict: It would move up materially if the seller produced the original manifolds/cats plus a specialist scan showing the only code is catalyst-efficiency, and the winning price left room for the OE catalyst restoration and street pads.

It would move up if a Porsche independent completed a pre-close borescope, leakdown and lift inspection with a clean report, and dated invoices surfaced for the water pump/thermostat and the PDK service.
It would move down further if the scan shows overrevs in ranges 4-6, misfire history, or PDK adaptation near limits — that would confirm the track-hardware inference.
It stays a no regardless if the hammer plus catalyst compliance, pads and tires puts it into the same money as a documented, unmodified manual example.
A manual 987.2 S with a specialist service binder at a similar price would displace this car outright.
evidence.mission_note: This fails the enthusiast_bridge brief on the transmission alone — PDK where a manual is required — and it does not earn the pragmatic_bridge exception, because a welded-in non-CARB catalyst setup with an illuminated CEL makes it neither convenient nor immediately usable in California, and there is no maintenance documentation to support the reliability case. In accelerated_bridge mode Jason should be buying evidence and easy resale, and this is a discount-tier, undocumented, modified car in the model's least differentiated colour combination.
evidence.rationale: This is a discount-tier example of an otherwise excellent model, and the disqualifiers are stated in the listing rather than inferred. The check engine light is on right now, caused by aftermarket high-flow catalytic converters welded into the factory manifold assemblies with no CARB EO; the seller confirms South Carolina has no inspections and that he never pursued a fix, which converts a cosmetic annoyance into a California registration project. It is a PDK where the mission requires a manual, and the profile is explicit that manual commands a widening premium while PDK cars sell slower — bad for the 6-24 month exit. Documentation is close to nil on the half that matters: the seller wrote 'I do not have any other service records,' the 2022 PDK service, plugs and annual oil changes are his own home-shop recollection, and a direct bidder question about the water pump and cooling system produced nothing at 83k miles and 16 years. The hardware set — Bilstein PSS9 coilovers, Tarett rear toe links, harness bar, Hawk HP Plus track pads on slotted rotors — is exactly what the profile flags as track-history signature, and the seller can only vouch for his own four years and 8k miles. Tires are mismatched Michelin front and Continental rear with no DOT dates. The car does present cleanly in the photos, the underside shot of the rear subframe looks dry and undamaged, the seller is candid and responsive, and the DFI 3.4 with LSD and Sport Chrono is genuinely the right engine — but with the auction closing in about a day there is no realistic path to a Porsche-specialist borescope, leakdown and scan before money moves.
evidence.next_action: Do not bid; if Jason wants to stay engaged, post one public question asking whether the original OEM manifolds/cats are included and requesting a photo of the scan tool showing the exact DTC and readiness status, and let the auction close without him unless a specialist PPI can be completed before it ends.

mission_fit.rationale: Body-on-frame V8, real 4WD, roof rack and a big square cargo area do serve dogs, gear, a sleeping platform or a rooftop tent, and an automatic is fine for this branch. Documentation of the 07/24/2026 minor damage (estimate and invoice) showing bumper-cover-only work, plus paint-depth readings confirming no structural repair.
A clean underbody/frame inspection after the Alaska years, and a matched set of four current-date-code tires (or a price concession to fit one).

Confirmation that the cooling system, transmission, transfer case and differentials have never been serviced would justify pricing the full fluid catch-up into the offer; refusal to allow a PPI before funds release through PSX should end it.
Any evidence that the gauge swing is a real thermal event (head gasket, water pump, thermostat) or that the cluster was swapped would take this off the list entirely.
evidence.mission_note: As a utility_capability candidate this GX earns its place next to the RX 350 on capability the crossover cannot supply — body-on-frame 4WD with low range, factory towing, roof rails for a tent or platform and a fold-flat third row — with Toyota/Lexus mechanicals the buyer's mechanic supports and an easy 367-mile fetch from Carmel. In accelerated_bridge mode the documentation depth and fresh suspension/brake work are attractive, but this is only a buy after the undiagnosed temperature-gauge and light-flicker complaint is cleared by an independent specialist; the low odometer must not be allowed to substitute for that answer.
evidence.rationale: Result: a genuinely interesting, heavily documented low-mileage GX that is not buyable as advertised until one specific undiagnosed symptom is resolved. The gold-tier evidence is excellent — a purchased CARFAX with 28 service records and the Lexus owner portal's verbatim repair orders — and it confirms the seller's best claims: front struts replaced 01/2026 at 60,972 mi, rear shocks 07/2026 at 63,175 mi, front pads/rotors 08/2025, rear pads and rotors 02/2026 and again 07/2026, oil at 63,175 mi, repeated alignments, 63,363 verified miles with no rollback indication and a CARFAX-guaranteed clean title. The same documents also contradict the page: CARFAX logs 'minor damage' on 07/24/2026 while Autotrader's blurb says no accident or damage reported, and the claimed four AT tires of 6/6/2026 do not appear anywhere in records that instead show tires fitted in four separate batches. Most importantly, the Lexus Escondido order of 08/07/2026 records the owner describing the temperature gauge swinging hot to cold with the lights flickering on an uphill turn and then declining the inspection — no scan, no diagnosis, and the car listed four weeks later, on an engine family known for valley-plate coolant leaks with no coolant service in any reported record. Add the BAR case over post-repair noise, the unresolved 'is this cluster original' question and seven Alaska winters with no underbody evidence, and the pre-sale picture is a cluster of loose ends rather than a tidy handover. Price at $25,040 is fair against the $24,420 CARFAX value and cheap against low-mile dealer asks, but this is a Base/Convenience car and the open items are worth a concession. Secondary air injection, KDSS and rust all sit in the unknown column; clean smog passes through 04/2025 are reassurance, not proof.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller to request the full Lexus Escondido RO 3410796 with the declined temperature-gauge/flicker line, a cold-start and uphill-turn video with the cluster in frame, and agreement to an independent Toyota/Lexus specialist PPI in Palm Desert with PSX funds held until it clears.

documentation.rationale: Everything material is seller prose: 'FULLY SERVICED', 'REAR BRAKE JOB', '1 ORIGINAL OWNER', 'AMAZING SHAPE'. No service receipts, no build/alignment invoices, no attached history report, no scan data, no odometer photo. The only third-party support is an Autotrader history badge summary. For a 126k-mile 1UR-FE truck whose two big-ticket risks (secondary air injection, KDSS) are both diagnostic questions, this is thin.

condition.rationale: The visible car presents well: straight silver bodywork, clean bronze Method wheels with a matched set of deep-tread KO3s, GOBI rack fitted squarely, no obvious damage in the two photos that are actually this vehicle. Brand-new ICON suspension and a rear brake job (claimed) address two normal wear areas. But 126k miles with no evidence on air-injection codes, KDSS lean, valley-plate/timing-cover seepage, transfer-case actuator, or original bushings/ball joints leaves the expensive half of the car unexamined, and the fresh lift can mask worn steering and driveline components on a short test drive.

price_value.rationale: $31,995 for a 126k-mile base-trim 2014 is out of line with the buyer's own comps: a 63.5k-mile 2013 Convenience AWD asks $25,040 in Palm Desert and a 128.5k-mile 2017 Premium asks $23,900; a 142.9k-mile 2010 sold for $14,250. The dealer's own board shows a 124k-mile 2014 at $29,995 and a 147k-mile 2015 at $27,995, so this unit is priced at the top of its own lot. The premium is entirely the ICON/GOBI/ARB build, which is dealer-installed cost that does not return at resale, and the asking price alone exceeds Jason's $27,000 max before tax, registration, or any catch-up work — all-in lands near the $33,000 defeats-purpose line.

mission_fit.rationale: As capability, this is genuinely what the RX 350 cannot do: body-on-frame, full-time 4WD with locking center diff, 285/70R17 A/Ts, roof rack and awning for dogs, gear and light camping — the mission brief's exact target. But it is also a second big Lexus SUV, and the catch-up note warns of RX overlap; it justifies itself only on off-road/overland character. Paying a modified-truck premium to add that character, while the BMW replacement budget is what is actually under pressure, weakens the fit rather than the concept.

logistics.rationale: San Diego is roughly 455 miles from Carmel — a comfortable fly-or-drive day, and a good car drives itself home on new tires. It is an established storefront dealer with published address and hours, so an independent PPI at a San Diego Toyota/Lexus specialist should be arrangeable, though the listing never states it. In-state CA sale means the dealer must furnish a smog certificate and registration transfer is straightforward. Dealer fees are stated as included in the price.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Silver over black leather with bronze Method wheels, a GOBI stealth rack and an ARB awning is a coherent, tasteful overland look, and ICON is quality hardware rather than a cheap spacer lift. It has real character and would be a pleasant, torquey, quiet thing to own. But it is explicitly not the enthusiast brief — automatic, heavy, 15 mpg city — and it is somebody else's build bought at retail rather than a spec Jason chose.

positives: Genuine capability the RX 350 does not supply: body-on-frame J150 platform, full-time 4WD with lockable center diff, 285/70R17 BFG KO3 all-terrains, GOBI rack and ARB awning for dogs, gear and light camping.

ppi_focus: Full-system scan with freeze-frame and readiness-monitor status; specifically interrogate the secondary air injection circuit and check for recently cleared codes.
Cold-start observation of the air injection pump cycle and audible check for the pump/valve failure pattern.
Confirm KDSS presence; if present, measure cross-corner lean and inspect the accumulators, lines and valve body for hydraulic weeping after the lift.
Inspect the 1UR-FE valley plate and timing-cover area for coolant/oil seepage, plus water pump and radiator condition.
Post-lift geometry and wear check: ICON uniball UCAs, ball joints, tie rods, steering rack, front lower control-arm bushings, and driveshaft/CV angles.
Transfer case actuator operation — cycle 4LO and center-diff lock, verify no fault, and check for gear-oil leakage.
Underbody and frame inspection for rust, impact damage, skid-plate contact, and any evidence of a removed hitch or tow wear.
Verify tire DOT date codes on all four KO3s and confirm even wear pattern consistent with a correct alignment.
Rear brake job verification (pad/rotor thickness and hardware) and front brake remaining life.
Transmission fluid condition and shift quality on a loaded highway test drive from cold.
what_would_change_verdict: A negotiated out-the-door price near the $25,000–$26,000 comp band, plus receipts, would bring the all-in inside budget and make this a serious utility candidate.
A clean full-system scan with all monitors ready plus a documented secondary-air-injection repair (or a written dealer warranty on it) would remove the biggest single cost risk.
KDSS confirmation with a measured lean of under ~1 inch and no hydraulic weeping, plus a KDSS-correct ICON install invoice and alignment sheet, would validate the build.
Discovery of stored or recently cleared P2440/P2442 codes, a KDSS lean, or valley-plate coolant seepage at PPI would end it at this price.
Refusal to allow an off-site independent PPI or to release the full history report would end it regardless of price.
evidence.mission_note: As pure capability this is exactly the utility_capability brief — a lifted, rack-and-awning GX460 does dogs, gear and light off-road duty the RX 350 cannot — but it is a second large Lexus SUV bought at a builder's retail premium, and at $31,995 it consumes the budget that is actually needed to retire the 335i. In accelerated_bridge mode it only makes sense at a materially lower out-the-door number with the air-injection and KDSS questions answered on paper.
evidence.rationale: The blocking issue is price, not the car: $31,995 for a base-trim 2014 with 126,000 miles sits above every relevant comp — a 63.5k-mile 2013 Convenience at $25,040, a 128.5k-mile 2017 Premium at $23,900, and the dealer's own 124k-mile 2014 at $29,995 — and it exceeds Jason's $27,000 max before tax and registration. The premium is a dealer-installed ICON Stage 2 / GOBI / ARB / Method build; the parts are quality and the photos corroborate the lift, matched bronze wheels and fresh KO3s, but that money does not come back at resale. Documentation is the other weakness: 'FULLY SERVICED', 'REAR BRAKE JOB', '1 ORIGINAL OWNER' and 'AMAZING SHAPE' are all seller prose with no receipts, no attached history report, no odometer photo and no scan data. Both model-critical mechanical questions are entirely unaddressed — secondary air injection (P2440/P2442, expensive and a California smog-fail item) and KDSS lean/leak status, which matters doubly because a Stage 2 lift on a KDSS chassis requires the KDSS-specific kit. Rust is likely a non-issue given San Diego provenance, but that is inference from location, not an underbody inspection, and no frame photos were captured. Logistics are the strong point: 455 in-state miles, a storefront dealer who must supply smog, and a straightforward PPI at a San Diego specialist. Mission-wise it delivers real capability the RX 350 lacks, but it is a second big Lexus SUV purchased at the top of its market while the 335i replacement budget is the actual constraint. Worth a scan-and-receipts conversation; not worth $31,995.
evidence.next_action: Email Miramar Motorsports asking for a cold full-system OBD scan photo with readiness monitors, the ICON install and service invoices, the full Carfax PDF, and written confirmation that an off-site independent PPI is allowed — and open at an out-the-door number in the $25,000–$26,000 range consistent with the comps.

What exactly did your 'inspected and reconditioned' process include on this car — please send the internal reconditioning work order.
Is the title clean and in the dealership's name, and can you email the full Carfax or AutoCheck PDF rather than the summary panel?
Please send photos of the odometer, the full interior including the shifter and pedals, the engine bay access panel, and all four tire sidewalls showing DOT date codes.
Can you send a cold-start video with sound, at least 60 seconds, plus a rear view at idle and on a light throttle blip to show any smoke?
What is the current coolant level in the expansion tank, and has the car ever shown a low-coolant warning or required top-ups while in your inventory?
What is the complete out-the-door price to a California buyer, including doc fee, and how do you handle temporary registration for a drive-home?
Are there any stored or pending fault codes, and will you provide a scan printout dated within the last week?
ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders, with special attention and retained photos for cylinders 4-6, looking for M97 bore scoring/varnish scuffing
DME over-rev report and full fault-code scan, including readiness monitors for a CA smog pass
Cold compression and leakdown, interpreted alongside (never instead of) the borescope
Cooling system pressure test: expansion tank, radiators, front-mounted coolant lines and any weeping at the water pump
AOS function test (vacuum check) and exhaust smoke observation on cold start and after a heat cycle
Clutch engagement point, flywheel condition/noise on idle, and rear main seal / IMS flange area for oil seepage
Front and rear suspension bushings, control-arm ball joints, and evidence of prior accident repair on the front-end panels shown in the photo
Tire date codes and brand matching across the 19in Carrera Classic wheels; wheel lip damage
Brake pad thickness, rotor wear ridges and brake fluid age
Undercarriage and inner-structure inspection for any unreported damage, since the history report only shows a no-event record
what_would_change_verdict: A dated, independent Porsche-specialist borescope with clean photos of cylinders 4-6 plus a clean DME over-rev report would move this from unbuyable to genuinely interesting.
A negotiated out-the-door price in the high $20,000s, backed by the $27,500 Encinitas sold comp, would bring it near budget — but still above Jason's stated maximum.
A folder of dated receipts covering water pump, coolant pipes, AOS and clutch, plus a clean title copy, would lift documentation from near-zero.
Any refusal to allow an outside specialist borescope before funds move, or any evidence of bore scoring, over-revs in range 4-6, or coolant loss, ends it immediately.
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper the specification is right — Cobalt Blue manual Cayman S with the good options — but at $35,900 it exceeds Jason's $33,000 defeats-purpose all-in and drains the cash he needs to replace the failing 335i, and it is an M97 3.4 offered with zero engine due diligence, which the profile marks as a hard stop. This is not a bridge car and cannot be justified in accelerated_bridge mode at this price without a clean borescope and a materially lower number.
evidence.rationale: Pass at the asking price. The single hard requirement for a 987 Cayman S — an independent Porsche-specialist borescope of cylinders 4-6 with retained photos — is entirely absent, as are the DME over-rev report and any cooling/AOS/water-pump documentation; the only engine evidence offered is the phrase 'Runs and drives great', which the profile explicitly says is not evidence of clean cylinder walls. Documentation is effectively nil: no receipts, no title statement, no history-report copy, no odometer or interior photo of this car (only one of the attached photos, the cobalt-blue car, plausibly depicts it; the rest are other inventory), and the dealer's 'inspected and reconditioned, as necessary' boilerplate names no part, date or mileage. Price is the second problem: $35,900 is at the top of the asking band and far above the recent transactions — $27,500 for a 28,400-mile 2007 S in Encinitas, $23,250 for a high-mile 2006 S — and it sits above Jason's $27,000 maximum and $33,000 defeats-purpose all-in before AZ dealer fees, tax and CA registration. The car itself looks cosmetically clean in the one relevant photo and the spec is genuinely desirable, and logistics are workable: a Tempe dealer lot means a Phoenix Porsche specialist can scope it before money moves. But paying a top-of-market S premium for an undocumented M97 while the 335i still needs replacing is exactly the outcome the mission brief warns against. Nothing here is a disclosed fault, so there is no known-work figure — the risk is unpriced, not proven.
evidence.next_action: Email Plaza Motors asking, in one message, whether they will release the car to a named independent Phoenix Porsche specialist for a full PPI including a six-cylinder borescope and a DME over-rev report at Jason's expense before any deposit — and treat anything other than an unqualified yes, plus an out-the-door number under $29,000, as a pass.

Eibach Pro-Truck Lift Stage 2R named in the ad; photos show an even, level ride height at all four corners with no rear sag and no obvious cheap spacer-lift geometry.
